questions.text: If the domain of the function $\log_5(18x-x^2-77)$ is $(\alpha, \beta)$ and the domain of the function $\log_{(x-1)}\left(\dfrac{2x^2+3x-2}{x^2-3x-4}\right)$ is $(\gamma, \delta)$, then $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$18x-x^2-77>0\iff(x-7)(x-11)<0$: $(\alpha,\beta)=(7,11)$.
Base: $x>1$, $x\neq2$. Argument $\dfrac{(2x-1)(x+2)}{(x-4)(x+1)}>0$; for $x>1$ this needs $x>4$. So $\gamma=4$.
$\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=49+121+16=186$.

questions.text:
Let $S=\mathbf{N}\cup\{0\}$. Define a relation R from S to $\mathbf{R}$ by :
$R=\left\{(x, y):\log_ey=x\log_e\left(\dfrac25\right), x\in S, y\in\mathbf{R}\right\}$.
Then, the sum of all the elements in the range of R is equal to :
questions.sol:
$y=\left(\tfrac25\right)^x$ for $x=0,1,2,\ldots$
Sum of the range $=\dfrac{1}{1-2/5}=\dfrac53$.

questions.text: Let $A=[a_{ij}]$ be a matrix of order $3\times3$, with $a_{ij}=\left(\sqrt2\right)^{i+j}$. If the sum of all the elements in the third row of $A^2$ is $\alpha+\beta\sqrt2$, $\alpha, \beta\in\mathbf{Z}$, then $\alpha+\beta$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$A=uu^T$ with $u=(\sqrt2,2,2\sqrt2)^T$, so $A^2=(u^Tu)A=14A$.
Third row sum of $A$: $2\sqrt2(\sqrt2+2+2\sqrt2)=12+4\sqrt2$.
For $A^2$: $14(12+4\sqrt2)=168+56\sqrt2$, so $\alpha+\beta=224$.

questions.text: Bag 1 contains 4 white balls and 5 black balls, and Bag 2 contains n white balls and 3 black balls. One ball is drawn randomly from Bag 1 and transferred to Bag 2. A ball is then drawn randomly from Bag 2. If the probability, that the ball drawn is white, is 29/45, then n is equal to :
questions.sol:
$P(\text{white})=\dfrac49\cdot\dfrac{n+1}{n+4}+\dfrac59\cdot\dfrac{n}{n+4}=\dfrac{9n+4}{9(n+4)}=\dfrac{29}{45}$.
$45n+20=29n+116\Rightarrow n=6$.

questions.text: Let $A=[a_{ij}]$ be a $2\times2$ matrix such that $a_{ij}\in\{0, 1\}$ for all $i$ and $j$. Let the random variable X denote the possible values of the determinant of the matrix A. Then, the variance of X is :
questions.sol:
There are 16 equally likely matrices; $\det=ad-bc\in\{-1,0,1\}$.
$\det=1$ needs $a=d=1$ and $bc=0$: 3 matrices; similarly $\det=-1$: 3 matrices; the other 10 give 0.
$E(X)=0$, $E(X^2)=\dfrac{6}{16}$, so $\operatorname{Var}(X)=\dfrac38$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the line $x+y=1$ meet the axes of $x$ and $y$ at A and B, respectively. A right angled triangle AMN is inscribed in the triangle OAB, where O is the origin and the points M and N lie on the lines OB and AB, respectively. If the area of the triangle AMN is $\dfrac49$ of the area of the triangle OAB and AN : NB $=\lambda:1$, then the sum of all possible value(s) of is $\lambda$ :
questions.sol:
$A=(1,0)$, $B=(0,1)$, and $N=\left(\dfrac{1}{1+\lambda},\dfrac{\lambda}{1+\lambda}\right)$. With the right angle at N, MN is perpendicular to AB, so M is where the line through N with slope 1 meets the $y$-axis: $M=\left(0,\dfrac{\lambda-1}{\lambda+1}\right)$, which lies on OB only if $\lambda\ge1$.
$AN=\dfrac{\sqrt2\lambda}{1+\lambda}$, $MN=\dfrac{\sqrt2}{1+\lambda}$, so area $=\dfrac{\lambda}{(1+\lambda)^2}=\dfrac49\cdot\dfrac12$.
$2\lambda^2-5\lambda+2=0\Rightarrow\lambda=2$ or $\tfrac12$; only $\lambda=2$ keeps M on OB. Sum $=2$.

questions.text: Let a circle C pass through the points (4, 2) and (0, 2), and its centre lie on $3x+2y+2=0$. Then the length of the chord, of the circle C, whose mid-point is (1, 2), is :
questions.sol:
The centre is on $x=2$ (perpendicular bisector of the two points) and on $3x+2y+2=0$: centre $(2,-4)$, $r^2=4+36=40$.
Distance from the centre to $(1,2)$: $\sqrt{37}$. Half-chord $=\sqrt{40-37}=\sqrt3$, chord $=2\sqrt3$.

questions.text: If $\alpha x+\beta y=109$ is the equation of the chord of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{9}+\dfrac{y^2}{4}=1$, whose mid point is $\left(\dfrac52, \dfrac12\right)$, then $\alpha+\beta$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Chord with given midpoint: $T=S_1$, i.e. $\dfrac{5x}{18}+\dfrac{y}{8}=\dfrac{25}{36}+\dfrac{1}{16}$.
Multiplying by 144: $40x+18y=109$, so $\alpha+\beta=58$.

questions.text:
If $\sin x+\sin^2x=1$, $x\in\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, then
$(\cos^{12}x+\tan^{12}x)+3(\cos^{10}x+\tan^{10}x+\cos^8x+\tan^8x)+(\cos^6x+\tan^6x)$
is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\sin x=1-\sin^2x=\cos^2x$, and $\tan^2x=\dfrac{\sin^2x}{\cos^2x}=\sin x$. So $\cos^2x=\tan^2x=s$ with $s+s^2=1$.
The expression is $2(s^6+3s^5+3s^4+s^3)=2s^3(1+s)^3=2(s+s^2)^3=2$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $\hat{a}$ be a unit vector perpendicular to the vectors $\vec{b}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, and makes an angle of $\cos^{-1}\left(-\dfrac13\right)$ with the vector $\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$. If $\hat{a}$ makes an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with the vector $\hat{i}+\alpha\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, then the value of $\alpha$ is :
questions.sol:
$\vec b\times\vec c=(-7,7,7)$, so $\hat a=\pm\dfrac{(-1,1,1)}{\sqrt3}$. The angle condition with $(1,1,1)$ needs $\hat a\cdot\dfrac{(1,1,1)}{\sqrt3}=-\tfrac13$, so $\hat a=\dfrac{(1,-1,-1)}{\sqrt3}$.
$\hat a\cdot(1,\alpha,1)=\dfrac{-\alpha}{\sqrt3}=\tfrac12\sqrt{2+\alpha^2}$, which needs $\alpha<0$ and $4\alpha^2=3(2+\alpha^2)$: $\alpha=-\sqrt6$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let a straight line L pass through the point P(2, $-1$, 3) and be perpendicular to the lines $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y+1}{1}=\dfrac{z-3}{-2}$ and $\dfrac{x-3}{1}=\dfrac{y-2}{3}=\dfrac{z+2}{4}$. If the line L intersects the $yz$-plane at the point Q, then the distance between the points P and Q is :
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
Let P be the foot of the perpendicular from the point (1, 2, 2) on the line L : $\dfrac{x-1}{1}=\dfrac{y+1}{-1}=\dfrac{z-2}{2}$.
Let the line $\vec{r}=\left(-\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\right)+\lambda\left(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}\right)$, $\lambda\in\mathbf{R}$, intersect the line L at Q. Then $2(PQ)^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
A point of L is $(1+t,-1-t,2+2t)$. Foot: $(t,-3-t,2t)\cdot(1,-1,2)=6t+3=0$, $t=-\tfrac12$, $P=\left(\tfrac12,-\tfrac12,1\right)$.
Intersection: $-1+\lambda=1+t$, $1-\lambda=-1-t$, $-2+\lambda=2+2t$ give $t=-2$, $\lambda=0$: $Q=(-1,1,-2)$.
$PQ^2=\tfrac94+\tfrac94+9=\tfrac{27}{2}$, so $2PQ^2=27$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the function $f(x)=(x^2-1)|x^2-ax+2|+\cos|x|$ be not differentiable at the two points $x=\alpha=2$ and $x=\beta$. Then the distance of the point $(\alpha, \beta)$ from the line $12x+5y+10=0$ is equal to :
questions.note: Dropped in the official final key (marks to all). With $\alpha=2$ the only other zero of $x^2-ax+2$ is $x=1$, where $f$ is differentiable, so the stated two points do not exist. The answer shown (3, taking $\beta=1$) is only a placeholder.
questions.sol:
$\cos|x|=\cos x$ is differentiable. Non-differentiability can come only from the zeros of $x^2-ax+2$ where $x^2-1\neq0$.
$x=2$ a zero gives $a=3$, and the other zero is $x=1$; there the factor $x^2-1$ vanishes, so $f$ is differentiable at 1 and there is no second point.
Taking $\beta=1$ anyway, the distance of $(2,1)$ from the line is $\dfrac{24+5+10}{13}=3$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the area enclosed between the curves $|y|=1-x^2$ and $x^2+y^2=1$ be $\alpha$. If $9\alpha=\beta\pi+\gamma$; $\beta$, $\gamma$ are integers, then the value of $|\beta-\gamma|$ equals.
questions.sol:
The curve $|y|=1-x^2$ lies inside the unit circle and meets it at $(\pm1,0)$ and $(0,\pm1)$.
Area inside it $=2\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1}(1-x^2)dx=\dfrac83$, so $\alpha=\pi-\dfrac83$.
$9\alpha=9\pi-24$: $\beta=9$, $\gamma=-24$, $|\beta-\gamma|=33$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If for the solution curve $y=f(x)$ of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+(\tan x)y=\dfrac{2+\sec x}{(1+2\sec x)^2}$, $x\in\left(\dfrac{-\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{10}$, then $f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Integrating factor $\sec x$: $\dfrac{d}{dx}(y\sec x)=\dfrac{\sec x(2+\sec x)}{(1+2\sec x)^2}=\dfrac{1+2\cos x}{(2+\cos x)^2}$.
Since $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{\sin x}{2+\cos x}\right)=\dfrac{1+2\cos x}{(2+\cos x)^2}$, $y\sec x=\dfrac{\sin x}{2+\cos x}+C$.
At $\tfrac\pi3$: $\dfrac{\sqrt3}{10}\cdot2=\dfrac{\sqrt3/2}{5/2}+C\Rightarrow C=0$, so $y=\dfrac{\sin x\cos x}{2+\cos x}$.
$f\left(\tfrac\pi4\right)=\dfrac{1/2}{2+1/\sqrt2}=\dfrac{1}{4+\sqrt2}=\dfrac{4-\sqrt2}{14}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let integers $a, b\in[-3, 3]$ be such that $a+b\neq0$. Then the number of all possible ordered pairs $(a, b)$, for which $\left|\dfrac{z-a}{z+b}\right|=1$ and $\begin{vmatrix}z+1&\omega&\omega^2\\\omega&z+\omega^2&1\\\omega^2&1&z+\omega\end{vmatrix}=1$, $z\in\mathbf{C}$, where $\omega$ and $\omega^2$ are the roots of $x^2+x+1=0$, is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Adding all rows to the first, each entry becomes $z$ (as $1+\omega+\omega^2=0$); the determinant then works out to $z^3$. So $z^3=1$: $z=1,\omega,\omega^2$.
$|z-a|=|z+b|$ means $z$ is on the perpendicular bisector of $a$ and $-b$, the line $\operatorname{Re}z=\dfrac{a-b}{2}$.
$z=1$: $a-b=2$, giving 4 pairs once $(1,-1)$ is excluded. $z=\omega,\omega^2$: $a-b=-1$, giving 6 pairs (none with $a+b=0$).
Total $=10$.

questions.text: Let $y^2=12x$ be the parabola and S be its focus. Let PQ be a focal chord of the parabola such that $(SP)(SQ)=\dfrac{147}{4}$. Let C be the circle described taking PQ as a diameter. If the equation of a circle C is $64x^2+64y^2-\alpha x-64\sqrt3y=\beta$, then $\beta-\alpha$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Take $P(3t^2,6t)$ and $Q\left(\tfrac{3}{t^2},-\tfrac6t\right)$. $SP\cdot SQ=9\left(t+\tfrac1t\right)^2=\tfrac{147}{4}$, so $t^2+\tfrac1{t^2}=\tfrac{25}{12}$ and $\left(t-\tfrac1t\right)^2=\tfrac1{12}$.
Circle on PQ: $x^2+y^2-(x_1+x_2)x-(y_1+y_2)y+x_1x_2+y_1y_2=0$ with $x_1+x_2=\tfrac{25}{4}$, $x_1x_2=9$, $y_1y_2=-36$, $y_1+y_2=6\left(t-\tfrac1t\right)=\sqrt3$ (sign matching the given equation).
$\times64$: $64x^2+64y^2-400x-64\sqrt3y=1728$, so $\beta-\alpha=1728-400=1328$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\lim_{t\to0}\left(\int_0^1(3x+5)^t\,dx\right)^{\frac1t}=\dfrac{\alpha}{5e}\left(\dfrac85\right)^{\frac23}$, then $\alpha$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
For small $t$, $(3x+5)^t\approx1+t\ln(3x+5)$, so the limit is $\exp\left(\displaystyle\int_0^1\ln(3x+5)dx\right)$.
$\displaystyle\int_0^1\ln(3x+5)dx=\tfrac13\left[u\ln u-u\right]_5^8=\tfrac13(8\ln8-5\ln5-3)$.
Limit $=\dfrac{8^{8/3}}{5^{5/3}e}=\dfrac{256}{5^{5/3}e}$, while the right side is $\dfrac{4\alpha}{5^{5/3}e}$. So $\alpha=64$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $24\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\left(\sin\left|4x-\frac{\pi}{12}\right|+[2\sin x]\right)dx=2\pi+\alpha$, where $[\cdot]$ denotes the greatest integer function, then $\alpha$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
On $\left[0,\tfrac\pi4\right]$, $[2\sin x]=1$ for $x\ge\tfrac\pi6$ and 0 before, so that part gives $\tfrac\pi4-\tfrac\pi6=\tfrac\pi{12}$.
With $u=4x-\tfrac\pi{12}$: $\tfrac14\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/12}^{11\pi/12}\sin|u|\,du=\tfrac14\left[(1-\cos\tfrac\pi{12})+(1+\cos\tfrac\pi{12})\right]=\tfrac12$.
$24\left(\tfrac12+\tfrac\pi{12}\right)=12+2\pi$, so $\alpha=12$.

questions.text: A sand dropper drops sand of mass m(t) on a conveyer belt at a rate proportional to the square root of speed $(v)$ of the belt, i.e. $\dfrac{dm}{dt}\propto\sqrt{v}$. If P is the power delivered to run the belt at constant speed then which of the following relationship is true ?
questions.sol:
Force needed to bring the falling sand up to the belt speed: $F=v\dfrac{dm}{dt}\propto v^{3/2}$.
$P=Fv\propto v^{5/2}$, so $P^2\propto v^5$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Three identical spheres of same mass undergo one dimensional motion as shown in figure with initial velocities $v_A=5$ m/s, $v_B=2$ m/s, $v_C=4$ m/s. If we wait sufficiently long for elastic collision to happen, then $v_A=4$ m/s, $v_B=2$ m/s, $v_C=5$ m/s will be the final velocities.
Reason (R) : In an elastic collision between identical masses, two objects exchange their velocities.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol:
R is true for a head-on elastic collision of equal masses.
A (5) catches B (2): they swap, giving $v_A=2$, $v_B=5$. B (5) catches C (4): they swap, giving $v_B=4$, $v_C=5$. Now $2<4<5$, so no more collisions.
Final velocities are $v_A=2$, $v_B=4$, $v_C=5$ m/s, not those stated, so A is false.

questions.text: Three equal masses m are kept at vertices (A, B, C) of an equilateral triangle of side a in free space. At t = 0, they are given an initial velocity $\vec{V}_A=V_0\overrightarrow{AC}$, $\vec{V}_B=V_0\overrightarrow{BA}$ and $\vec{V}_C=V_0\overrightarrow{CB}$. Here, $\overrightarrow{AC}$, $\overrightarrow{CB}$ and $\overrightarrow{BA}$ are unit vectors along the edges of the triangle. If the three masses interact gravitationally, then the magnitude of the net angular momentum of the system at the point of collision is :
questions.sol:
Gravity between the masses is internal, so angular momentum about the centroid is conserved.
Each velocity is along a side, at perpendicular distance $\dfrac{a}{2\sqrt3}$ (the inradius) from the centroid, all in the same sense.
$L=3mV_0\cdot\dfrac{a}{2\sqrt3}=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}amV_0$.

questions.text: A cup of coffee cools from 90°C to 80°C in t minutes when the room temperature is 20°C. The time taken by the similar cup of coffee to cool from 80°C to 60°C at the same room temperature is :
questions.sol:
Newton's law of cooling with average temperatures: $\dfrac{10}{t}=k(85-20)$ and $\dfrac{20}{t'}=k(70-20)$.
$\dfrac{t'}{t}=\dfrac{20/50}{10/65}=\dfrac{13}{5}$, so $t'=\dfrac{13}{5}t$.

questions.text: The difference of temperature in a material can convert heat energy into electrical energy. To harvest the heat energy, the material should have
options: high thermal conductivity and high electrical conductivity
low thermal conductivity and low electrical conductivity
high thermal conductivity and low electrical conductivity
low thermal conductivity and high electrical conductivity
questions.sol:
A thermoelectric generator needs a temperature difference to be kept across it, so heat should leak through slowly (low thermal conductivity).
The generated current should flow with little resistive loss (high electrical conductivity).

questions.text:
A poly-atomic molecule ($C_V=3R$, $C_P=4R$, where R is gas constant) goes from phase space point A($P_A=10^5$ Pa, $V_A=4\times10^{-6}$ m$^3$) to point B($P_B=5\times10^4$ Pa, $V_B=6\times10^{-6}$ m$^3$) to point C($P_C=10^4$ Pa, $V_C=8\times10^{-6}$ m$^3$). A to B is an adiabatic path and B to C is an isothermal path.
The net heat absorbed per unit mole by the system is :
questions.sol:
A to B is adiabatic: no heat.
B to C is isothermal at 450 K (from the graph): $Q=RT\ln\dfrac{V_C}{V_B}=450R\ln\dfrac86=450R(\ln4-\ln3)$ per mole.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : With the increase in the pressure of an ideal gas, the volume falls off more rapidly in an isothermal process in comparison to the adiabatic process.
Reason (R) : In isothermal process, PV = constant, while in adiabatic process $PV^\gamma$ = constant. Here $\gamma$ is the ratio of specific heats, P is the pressure and V is the volume of the ideal gas.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol:
From R: isothermal $\dfrac{dV}{dP}=-\dfrac VP$; adiabatic $\dfrac{dV}{dP}=-\dfrac{V}{\gamma P}$.
As $\gamma>1$, the volume falls faster with pressure in the isothermal process, so A follows directly from R.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two bodies A and B of equal mass are suspended from two massless springs of spring constant $k_1$ and $k_2$, respectively. If the bodies oscillate vertically such that their amplitudes are equal, the ratio of the maximum velocity of A to the maximum velocity of B is
questions.sol: $v_{\max}=A\omega=A\sqrt{k/m}$. With equal $A$ and $m$, $\dfrac{v_A}{v_B}=\sqrt{\dfrac{k_1}{k_2}}$.

questions.text: An electric dipole is placed at a distance of 2 cm from an infinite plane sheet having positive charge density $\sigma_o$. Choose the correct option from the following.
options: Torque on dipole is zero and net force acts towards the sheet.
Torque on dipole is zero and net force is directed away from the sheet.
Potential energy of dipole is minimum and torque is zero.
Potential energy and torque both are maximum.
questions.sol:
The sheet's field is uniform, $\dfrac{\sigma_o}{2\epsilon_0}$, directed away from the sheet.
The dipole points from $-q$ (near the sheet) to $+q$ (further away), i.e. along the field: $\theta=0$.
So $\tau=pE\sin\theta=0$ and $U=-pE\cos\theta$ is minimum; in a uniform field the net force is zero.

questions.text: A capacitor, $C_1=6$ $\mu$F is charged to a potential difference of $V_0=5$V using a 5V battery. The battery is removed and another capacitor, $C_2=12$ $\mu$F is inserted in place of the battery. When the switch 'S' is closed, the charge flows between the capacitors for some time until equilibrium condition is reached. What are the charges ($q_1$ and $q_2$) on the capacitors $C_1$ and $C_2$ when equilibrium condition is reached.
questions.sol:
Initial charge $Q=6\times5=30$ $\mu$C, shared until the voltages are equal.
$V=\dfrac{30}{6+12}=\dfrac53$ V, so $q_1=6\times\tfrac53=10$ $\mu$C and $q_2=12\times\tfrac53=20$ $\mu$C.

questions.text: A plane electromagnetic wave propagates along the $+x$ direction in free space. The components of the electric field, $\vec{E}$ and magnetic field, $\vec{B}$ vectors associated with the wave in Cartesian frame are
questions.sol:
$\vec E$ and $\vec B$ are perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel, with $\vec E\times\vec B$ along $+x$.
$E_y$ with $B_z$ gives $\hat j\times\hat k=\hat i$. ($E_z$ with $B_y$ would point along $-x$; $E_x$ or $B_x$ is impossible.)
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A convex lens made of glass (refractive index = 1.5) has focal length 24 cm in air. When it is totally immersed in water (refractive index = 1.33), its focal length changes to
questions.sol:
Lens maker's formula: $\dfrac{f_w}{f_a}=\dfrac{1.5-1}{\frac{1.5}{1.33}-1}$.
With $1.33\approx\tfrac43$: $\dfrac{0.5}{1.125-1}=4$, so $f_w=4\times24=96$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two identical symmetric double convex lenses of focal length $f$ are cut into two equal parts $L_1$, $L_2$ by AB plane and $L_3$, $L_4$ by XY plane as shown in figure respectively. The ratio of focal lengths of lenses $L_1$ and $L_3$ is
questions.sol:
Cutting along AB (a plane containing the principal axis) leaves each half with both curved faces: focal length still $f$.
Cutting along XY (the plane of the lens) gives plano-convex halves, each with half the power: focal length $2f$.
Ratio $f:2f=1:2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two concave refracting surfaces of equal radii of curvature and refractive index 1.5 face each other in air as shown in figure. A point object O is placed midway, between P and B. The separation between the images of O, formed by each refracting surface is :
questions.sol:
From the figure, $AP=R$ and $OB=R/2$ with O midway between P and B, so $OA=\tfrac{3R}{2}$. Each surface has its centre of curvature on the air side, so $R$ is negative in $\dfrac{\mu_2}{v}-\dfrac{\mu_1}{u}=\dfrac{\mu_2-\mu_1}{R}$.
Surface B: $\dfrac{1.5}{v}+\dfrac{2}{R}=-\dfrac{0.5}{R}\Rightarrow v=-0.6R$: image $0.6R$ from B, i.e. $0.4R$ from P.
Surface A: $\dfrac{1.5}{v}+\dfrac{2}{3R}=-\dfrac{0.5}{R}\Rightarrow v=-\tfrac97R\approx-1.286R$: image $1.286R$ from A, i.e. $0.286R$ from P.
Separation $\approx0.400R-0.286R=0.114R$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The number of spectral lines emitted by atomic hydrogen that is in the 4<sup>th</sup> energy level, is
questions.sol: From $n=4$, transitions between any two of the levels 4, 3, 2, 1 are possible: $\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}=6$ lines.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In an experiment with photoelectric effect, the stopping potential,
options: increases with increase in the wavelength of the incident light
decreases with increase in the intensity of the incident light
increases with increase in the intensity of the incident light
is $\left(\dfrac1e\right)$ times the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons
questions.sol:
$eV_0=K_{\max}$, so $V_0=\dfrac{K_{\max}}{e}$.
$V_0$ falls as $\lambda$ rises ($K_{\max}=hc/\lambda-\phi$) and does not depend on intensity.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: The truth table for the circuit given below is :
questions.sol:
One AND gate receives A and $\bar B$, the other $\bar A$ and B; the OR gate gives $Y=A\bar B+\bar AB$ (XOR).
So $Y=1$ only when exactly one input is 1: the table with outputs 0, 1, 1, 0 for $AB=00,01,10,11$ (option (1)).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A physical quantity Q is related to four observables a, b, c, d as follows :
$Q=\dfrac{ab^4}{cd}$
where, $a=(60\pm3)$Pa; $b=(20\pm0.1)$m; $c=(40\pm0.2)$Nsm$^{-2}$ and $d=(50\pm0.1)$m, then the percentage error in Q is $\dfrac{x}{1000}$, where $x$ = __________.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two cars P and Q are moving on a road in the same direction. Accleration of car P increases linearly with time whereas car Q moves with a constant accleration. Both cars cross each other at time t = 0, for the first time. The maximum possible number of crossing(s) (including the crossing at t = 0) is __________.
questions.sol:
With $a_P=\alpha+\beta t$ and $a_Q$ constant, the relative position $x_P-x_Q$ is a cubic in $t$ that vanishes at $t=0$.
A cubic has at most three real roots, so there can be at most 3 crossings (including $t=0$).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two planets, A and B are orbiting a common star in circular orbits of radii $R_A$ and $R_B$, respectively, with $R_B=2R_A$. The planet B is $4\sqrt2$ times more massive than planet A. The ratio $\left(\dfrac{L_B}{L_A}\right)$ of angular momentum $(L_B)$ of planet B to that of planet A$(L_A)$ is closest to integer __________.
questions.sol:
Orbital speed $v=\sqrt{GM/R}$, so $L=mvR=m\sqrt{GMR}$.
$\dfrac{L_B}{L_A}=4\sqrt2\times\sqrt2=8$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The magnetic field inside a 200 turns solenoid of radius 10 cm is $2.9\times10^{-4}$ Tesla. If the solenoid carries a current of 0.29 A, then the length of the solenoid is __________ $\pi$ cm.
questions.sol: $B=\dfrac{\mu_0NI}{l}\Rightarrow l=\dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times200\times0.29}{2.9\times10^{-4}}=0.08\pi$ m $=8\pi$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor consisting of two circular plates of radius 10 cm is being charged by a constant current of 0.15 A. If the rate of change of potential difference between the plates is $7\times10^8$ V/s then the integer value of the distance between the parallel plates is $\left(\text{Take, }\epsilon_0=9\times10^{-12}\dfrac{\text{F}}{\text{m}}, \pi=\dfrac{22}{7}\right)$ __________ $\mu$m.
questions.sol:
$I=C\dfrac{dV}{dt}\Rightarrow C=\dfrac{0.15}{7\times10^8}$ F.
$d=\dfrac{\epsilon_0A}{C}=\dfrac{9\times10^{-12}\times\frac{22}{7}\times0.01\times7\times10^8}{0.15}=1.32\times10^{-3}$ m $=1320$ $\mu$m.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
0.1 M solution of KI reacts with excess of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ and $\mathrm{KIO_3}$ solutions. According to equation
$\mathrm{5I^-+IO_3^-+6H^+\rightarrow3I_2+3H_2O}$
Identify the correct statements :
(A) 200 mL of KI solution reacts with 0.004 mol of $\mathrm{KIO_3}$
(B) 200 mL of KI solution reacts with 0.006 mol of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$
(C) 0.5 L of KI solution produced 0.005 mol of $\mathrm{I_2}$
(D) Equivalent weight of $\mathrm{KIO_3}$ is equal to $\left(\dfrac{\text{Molecular weight}}{5}\right)$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
200 mL of 0.1 M KI is 0.02 mol $\mathrm{I^-}$: it needs 0.004 mol $\mathrm{IO_3^-}$ (A true) and 0.024 mol $\mathrm{H^+}$, i.e. 0.012 mol $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ (B false).
0.5 L is 0.05 mol $\mathrm{I^-}$, giving 0.03 mol $\mathrm{I_2}$ (C false).
In $\mathrm{IO_3^-\rightarrow I_2}$ iodine goes from +5 to 0, so the equivalent weight is $M/5$ (D true).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : It is impossible to specify simultaneously with arbitrary precision, both the linear momentum and the position of a particle.
Statement (II) : If the uncertainty in the measurement of position and uncertainty in measurement of momentum are equal for an electron, then the uncertainty in the measurement of velocity is $\ge\sqrt{\dfrac{h}{\pi}}\times\dfrac{1}{2m}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
I is Heisenberg's uncertainty principle: correct.
II: $\Delta x\,\Delta p\ge\dfrac{h}{4\pi}$ with $\Delta x=\Delta p$ gives $\Delta p\ge\dfrac12\sqrt{\dfrac h\pi}$, so $\Delta v=\dfrac{\Delta p}{m}\ge\dfrac{1}{2m}\sqrt{\dfrac h\pi}$: correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
For hydrogen like species, which of the following graphs provides the most appropriate representation of E vs Z plot for a constant n ?
[E : Energy of the stationary state,
Z : atomic number, n = principal quantum number]
questions.sol: $E_n=-13.6\dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}$ eV, so at constant $n$ the energy is negative and falls as $Z^2$: a downward-opening parabola from the origin (graph (3)).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
If
C(diamond) $\rightarrow$ C(graphite) + X kJ mol$^{-1}$
C(diamond) + $\mathrm{O_2(g)\rightarrow CO_2(g)}$ + Y kJ mol$^{-1}$
C(graphite) + $\mathrm{O_2(g)\rightarrow CO_2(g)}$ + Z kJ mol$^{-1}$
at constant temperature. Then
questions.sol:
Burning diamond can be done in two steps: diamond to graphite (releases X), then graphite to $\mathrm{CO_2}$ (releases Z).
By Hess's law $Y=X+Z$, so $X=Y-Z$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : NaCl is added to the ice at 0°C, present in the ice cream box to prevent the melting of ice cream.
Statement (II) : On addition of NaCl to ice at 0°C, there is a depression in freezing point.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Salt lowers the freezing point of the water, so the ice-salt mixture stays liquid-solid well below 0 °C and keeps the ice cream frozen.
Both statements are correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the equilibrium
$\mathrm{CO(g)+3H_2(g)\rightleftharpoons CH_4(g)+H_2O(g)}$
If the pressure applied over the system increases by two fold at constant temperature then
(A) Concentration of reactants and products increases.
(B) Equilibrium will shift in forward direction.
(C) Equilibrium constant increases since concentration of products increases.
(D) Equilibrium constant remains unchanged as concentration of reactants and products remain same.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Compressing the gas raises every concentration (A true). The forward reaction reduces the number of gas moles (4 to 2), so the equilibrium shifts forward (B true).
K depends only on temperature, so it does not change; but the concentrations do change, so the reason in D is wrong, and C is wrong too.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
$\mathrm{O_2}$ gas will be evolved as a product of electrolysis of :
(A) an aqueous solution of $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ using silver electrodes.
(B) an aqueous solution of $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ using platinum electrodes.
(C) a dilute solution of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ using platinum electrodes.
(D) a high concentration solution of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ using platinum electrodes.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) A silver anode itself dissolves ($\mathrm{Ag\rightarrow Ag^++e^-}$): no oxygen.
(B) With inert Pt the anode oxidises water: $\mathrm{O_2}$ is evolved. (C) Dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ with Pt: water is oxidised to $\mathrm{O_2}$.
(D) Concentrated $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$: sulphate is oxidised to peroxodisulphate ($\mathrm{S_2O_8^{2-}}$) instead.
So (B) and (C) only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II :
List - I
Applications		List - II
Batteries/Cell
(A) Transistors(I) Anode - Zn/Hg ; Cathode - HgO + C
(B) Hearing aids(II) Hydrogen fuel cell
(C) Invertors(III) Anode - Zn ; Cathode - Carbon
(D) Apollo space ship(IV) Anode - Pb ; Cathode - Pb|PbO$_2$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Transistor radios use the dry (Leclanché) cell, Zn anode and carbon cathode (III).
Hearing aids use the mercury cell, Zn/Hg anode and HgO + C cathode (I).
Inverters use the lead storage battery (IV). The Apollo programme used hydrogen-oxygen fuel cells (II).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Drug X becomes ineffective after 50% decomposition. The original concentration of drug in a bottle was 16 mg/mL which becomes 4 mg/mL in 12 months. The expiry time of the drug in months is __________.
Assume that the decomposition of the drug follows first order kinetics.
questions.sol:
16 to 4 mg/mL is two half-lives in 12 months, so $t_{1/2}=6$ months.
The drug fails at 50% decomposition, i.e. after one half-life: 6 months.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The type of oxide formed by the element among Li, Na, Be, Mg, B and Al that has the least atomic radius is :
questions.sol:
Radius falls across a period and rises down a group, so boron is the smallest of these.
Boron is trivalent and forms $\mathrm{B_2O_3}$, type $\mathrm{A_2O_3}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text: First ionisation enthalpy values of first four group 15 elements are given below. Choose the correct value for the element that is a main component of apatite family :
questions.sol:
Apatites are calcium phosphates, so the element is phosphorus.
Down group 15 the first ionisation enthalpy falls: N 1402, P 1012, As 947, Sb 834 kJ mol$^{-1}$. P: 1012 kJ mol$^{-1}$.

questions.text: The calculated spin-only magnetic moments of $\mathrm{K_3[Fe(OH)_6]}$ and $\mathrm{K_4[Fe(OH)_6]}$ respectively are :
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{OH^-}$ is a weak-field ligand, so both are high spin.
$\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ ($d^5$): 5 unpaired, $\sqrt{35}=5.92$ B.M. $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ ($d^6$): 4 unpaired, $\sqrt{24}=4.90$ B.M.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Identify the homoleptic complexes with odd number of d electrons in the central metal :
(A) $\mathrm{[FeO_4]^{2-}}$
(B) $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}$
(C) $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_5NO]^{2-}}$
(D) $\mathrm{[CoCl_4]^{2-}}$
(E) $\mathrm{[Co(H_2O)_3F_3]}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Homoleptic (one kind of ligand): A, B and D. C and E have two kinds of ligand.
A: Fe(VI), $d^2$ (even). B: $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$, $d^5$ (odd). D: $\mathrm{Co^{2+}}$, $d^7$ (odd).
So B and D only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : In partition chromatography, stationary phase is thin film of liquid present in the inert support.
Statement (II) : In paper chromatography, the material of paper acts as a stationary phase.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
I is correct: partition chromatography uses a liquid film held on an inert support as the stationary phase.
II is wrong: paper chromatography is a form of partition chromatography, and the stationary phase is the water held in the paper, not the paper itself.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: Total number of sigma $(\sigma)$ __________ and pi$(\pi)$ __________ bonds respectively present in hex-1-en-4-yne are :
questions.sol:
Hex-1-en-4-yne is $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH-CH_2-C{\equiv}C-CH_3}$ ($\mathrm{C_6H_8}$).
$\sigma$: 5 C-C + 8 C-H $=13$. $\pi$: 1 (C=C) + 2 (C≡C) $=3$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : On nitration of m-xylene with $\mathrm{HNO_3}$, $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ followed by oxidation, 4-nitrobenzene-1,3-dicarboxylic acid is obtained as the major product.
Statement (II) : $-\mathrm{CH_3}$ group is o/p-directing while $-\mathrm{NO_2}$ group is m-directing group.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
In m-xylene both methyl groups direct to C-4 (ortho to one, para to the other), which is also less hindered than C-2, so nitration gives 1,3-dimethyl-4-nitrobenzene.
Oxidising both methyls gives 4-nitrobenzene-1,3-dicarboxylic acid: I is true.
II states the usual directing effects: true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which among the following halides will generate the most stable carbocation in the nucleophilic substitution reaction?
questions.sol:
Losing $\mathrm{Br^-}$ gives the triphenylmethyl, benzyl, allyl and cyclohex-2-enyl cations.
The triphenylmethyl cation is spread over three benzene rings and is by far the most stable (option (4)).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which one of the following, with HBr will give a phenol ?
questions.sol:
An aryl alkyl ether is cleaved by HBr at the alkyl-oxygen bond, because the aryl-oxygen bond has partial double bond character.
Anisole gives phenol and $\mathrm{CH_3Br}$ (option (2)); the benzyl ethers and the acetal give benzyl compounds, not phenol.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which one of the following reaction sequences will give an azo dye ?
questions.sol:
Nitrobenzene is reduced by Sn/HCl to aniline, which $\mathrm{NaNO_2}$/HCl converts to benzenediazonium chloride; coupling with alkaline $\beta$-naphthol gives an orange-red azo dye (option (2)).
The other sequences give an amide, a sulphonamide and, with aniline, a diazonium salt that does not couple with toluene.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Identify the essential amino acids from below :
(A) Valine
(B) Proline
(C) Lysine
(D) Threonine
(E) Tyrosine
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Valine, lysine and threonine are essential (they must come from the diet).
Proline and tyrosine are made in the body, so they are non-essential.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Total number of non bonded electrons present in $\mathrm{NO_2^-}$ ion based on Lewis theory is __________.
questions.sol:
Lewis structure $\mathrm{O{=}N-O^-}$ (18 valence electrons): N has one lone pair, the double-bonded O two, the single-bonded O three.
Lone pairs $=6$, i.e. 12 non-bonded electrons.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following low-spin complexes
$\mathrm{K_3[Co(NO_2)_6]}$, $\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}$, $\mathrm{K_3[Fe(CN)_6]}$, $\mathrm{Cu_2[Fe(CN)_6]}$ and $\mathrm{Zn_2[Fe(CN)_6]}$.
The sum of the spin-only magnetic moment values of complexes having yellow colour is __________ B.M. (answer in nearest integer)
questions.sol:
The yellow ones are $\mathrm{K_3[Co(NO_2)_6]}$ and $\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}$ (the ferricyanide is red, $\mathrm{Cu_2[Fe(CN)_6]}$ chocolate-brown, $\mathrm{Zn_2[Fe(CN)_6]}$ white).
Both contain low-spin $d^6$ ions ($\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$) with no unpaired electrons, so the sum is 0.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
In the sulphur estimation, 0.20 g of a pure organic compound gave 0.40 g of barium sulphate. The percentage of sulphur in the compound is __________ $\times10^{-1}$%.
(Molar mass : O = 16, S = 32, Ba = 137 in g mol$^{-1}$)
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{BaSO_4}$ has molar mass 233 and contains 32 g S per mole.
$\%\mathrm S=\dfrac{32}{233}\times\dfrac{0.40}{0.20}\times100=27.47\%\approx275\times10^{-1}\%$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
Isomeric hydrocarbons $\rightarrow$ negative Baeyer's test
(Molecular formula $\mathrm{C_9H_{12}}$)
The total number of isomers from above with four different non-aliphatic substitution sites is -
questions.sol:
A negative Baeyer's test (no C=C outside a ring) with $\mathrm{C_9H_{12}}$ means alkylbenzenes: propylbenzene, cumene, three ethyltoluenes and three trimethylbenzenes.
Count the distinct ring C-H positions: propylbenzene and cumene 3 each; o- and m-ethyltoluene 4 each; p-ethyltoluene 2; 1,2,3-, 1,2,4- and 1,3,5-trimethylbenzene 2, 3 and 1.
Only o- and m-ethyltoluene have four: 2 isomers.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: In the Claisen-Schmidt reaction to prepare, dibenzalacetone from 5.3 g of benzaldehyde, a total of 3.51 g of product was obtained. The percentage yield in this reaction was __________%.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{2C_6H_5CHO+CH_3COCH_3\rightarrow C_6H_5CH{=}CHCOCH{=}CHC_6H_5}$ (molar mass 234).
5.3 g benzaldehyde $=0.05$ mol, which can give 0.025 mol $=5.85$ g of product.
Yield $=\dfrac{3.51}{5.85}\times100=60\%$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
